411: @dataclass
412: class DateCandidate:
413:     """One date like column with its range, format, and order verdict."""
414: 
415:     column: str
416:     matched: int
417:     total: int
418:     kind: str  # iso, numeric, compact, datetime, or name
419:     format_label: str  # what the adapter should parse
420:     verdict: str  # ISO, DD/MM, MM/DD, ambiguous, compact, or unparsed
421:     dayfirst: bool
422:     start: str  # range start, empty when unparsed
423:     end: str  # range end, empty when unparsed
424:     proof: str = ""
425:     has_time: bool = False
426: 
427: 
428: def stamp_label(value: object) -> str:
429:     """Render a timestamp as a date when the time is midnight, else date time."""
430:     stamp = pd.Timestamp(value)
431:     if stamp.hour == 0 and stamp.minute == 0 and stamp.second == 0:
432:         return stamp.date().isoformat()
433:     return stamp.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
434: 
435: 
436: def range_labels(parsed: pd.Series, texts: pd.Series) -> tuple[str, str]:
437:     """Small to large range labels, falling back to string order when unparsed."""
438:     good = parsed.dropna()
439:     if len(good) > 0:
440:         return stamp_label(good.min()), stamp_label(good.max())
441:     return str(texts.min()), str(texts.max())
442: 
443: 
444: def iso_candidate(column: str, texts: pd.Series) -> DateCandidate:
445:     """A column of YYYY-MM-DD style values, with an optional time part."""
446:     parsed = pd.to_datetime(texts, errors="coerce", format="ISO8601")
447:     if bool(parsed.isna().all()):
448:         try:
449:             parsed = pd.to_datetime(texts, errors="coerce")
450:         except ValueError:
451:             parsed = pd.Series(pd.NaT, index=texts.index)
452:     start, end = range_labels(parsed, texts)
453:     return DateCandidate(
454:         column=column,
455:         matched=len(texts),
456:         total=len(texts),
457:         kind="iso",
458:         format_label="YYYY-MM-DD",
459:         verdict="ISO",
460:         dayfirst=False,
461:         start=start,
462:         end=end,
463:         proof="",
464:         has_time=bool(texts.str.contains(TIME_PART_RE).any()),
465:     )
466: 
467: 
468: def numeric_date_candidate(column: str, texts: pd.Series) -> DateCandidate:
469:     """Resolve DD/MM versus MM/DD: a first position value above 12 proves DD/MM."""
470:     parts = texts.str.extract(NUMERIC_DATE_RE)
471:     first = pd.to_numeric(parts.iloc[:, 0], errors="coerce")
472:     second = pd.to_numeric(parts.iloc[:, 1], errors="coerce")
473:     first_max = int(first.max()) if bool(first.notna().any()) else 0
474:     second_max = int(second.max()) if bool(second.notna().any()) else 0
475:     if first_max > 12 and second_max <= 12:
476:         verdict = "DD/MM"
477:         proof = f"first position value {first_max} proves day first"
478:     elif second_max > 12 and first_max <= 12:
479:         verdict = "MM/DD"
480:         proof = f"second position value {second_max} proves month first"
481:     elif first_max > 12 and second_max > 12:
482:         verdict = "ambiguous"
483:         proof = (
484:             f"both positions exceed 12 (first max {first_max}, second max "
485:             f"{second_max}), so the rows disagree"
486:         )
487:     else:
488:         verdict = "ambiguous"
489:         proof = (
490:             "every value is at most 12 in both positions, so a known date "
491:             "must break the tie"
492:         )
493:     dayfirst = verdict in {"DD/MM", "ambiguous"}
494:     format_label = {
495:         "DD/MM": "DD/MM/YYYY",
496:         "MM/DD": "MM/DD/YYYY",
497:         "ambiguous": "DD/MM/YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY",
498:     }[verdict]
499:     try:
500:         parsed = pd.to_datetime(
501:             texts, errors="coerce", dayfirst=dayfirst, format="mixed"
502:         )
503:     except ValueError:
504:         parsed = pd.Series(pd.NaT, index=texts.index)
505:     start, end = range_labels(parsed, texts)
506:     return DateCandidate(
507:         column=column,
508:         matched=len(texts),
509:         total=len(texts),
510:         kind="numeric",
511:         format_label=format_label,
512:         verdict=verdict,
513:         dayfirst=dayfirst,
514:         start=start,
515:         end=end,
516:         proof=proof,
517:         has_time=bool(texts.str.contains(TIME_PART_RE).any()),
518:     )
519: 
520: 
521: def compact_date_candidate(column: str, texts: pd.Series) -> DateCandidate:
522:     """Eight digit dates such as 20251101, with Excel serials as the other read."""
523:     numbers = pd.to_numeric(texts, errors="coerce")
524:     plausible_share = float(((numbers >= 19000101) & (numbers <= 20991231)).mean())
525:     if plausible_share >= MIN_DATE_MATCH_SHARE:
526:         parsed = pd.to_datetime(texts, errors="coerce", format="%Y%m%d")
527:         start, end = range_labels(parsed, texts)
528:         return DateCandidate(
529:             column=column,
530:             matched=len(texts),
531:             total=len(texts),
532:             kind="compact",
533:             format_label="YYYYMMDD",
534:             verdict="compact",
535:             dayfirst=False,
536:             start=start,
537:             end=end,
538:             proof="eight digit values inside the 19000101 to 20991231 band",
539:         )
540:     serial_share = float(((numbers >= 30000) & (numbers <= 60000)).mean())
541:     if serial_share >= MIN_DATE_MATCH_SHARE:
542:         proof = "values sit in the 30000 to 60000 band, which looks like Excel serial day numbers"
543:     else:
544:         proof = "values are eight digits but fall outside any plausible date range"
545:     return DateCandidate(
546:         column=column,
547:         matched=0,
548:         total=len(texts),
549:         kind="compact",
550:         format_label="undetermined",
551:         verdict="unparsed",
552:         dayfirst=False,
553:         start="",
554:         end="",
555:         proof=proof,
556:     )
557: 
558: 
559: def name_only_candidate(column: str, texts: pd.Series) -> DateCandidate:
560:     """The name says date but no value matches a known pattern: say why."""
561:     numbers = pd.to_numeric(texts, errors="coerce")
562:     numeric_share = float(numbers.notna().mean())
563:     serial_share = (
564:         float(((numbers >= 30000) & (numbers <= 60000)).mean())
565:         if numeric_share >= MIN_DATE_MATCH_SHARE
566:         else 0.0
567:     )
568:     if serial_share >= MIN_DATE_MATCH_SHARE:
569:         proof = "values look like Excel serial day numbers (the 30000 to 60000 band)"
570:     else:
571:         proof = "values match neither YYYY-MM-DD nor a slash date pattern"
572:     return DateCandidate(
573:         column=column,
574:         matched=0,
575:         total=len(texts),
576:         kind="name",
577:         format_label="undetermined",
578:         verdict="unparsed",
579:         dayfirst=False,
580:         start="",
581:         end="",
582:         proof=proof,
583:     )
584: 
585: 
586: def datetime_candidate(column: str, series: pd.Series) -> DateCandidate:
587:     """A column pandas already read as datetimes, typical of xlsx exports."""
588:     stamps = pd.to_datetime(series, errors="coerce")
589:     has_time = bool(
590:         ((stamps.dt.hour != 0) | (stamps.dt.minute != 0) | (stamps.dt.second != 0)).any()
591:     )
592:     start, end = range_labels(stamps, series.astype("string"))
593:     return DateCandidate(
594:         column=column,
595:         matched=len(series),
596:         total=len(series),
597:         kind="datetime",
598:         format_label="datetime64 (already parsed)",
599:         verdict="ISO",
600:         dayfirst=False,
601:         start=start,
602:         end=end,
603:         proof="workbook dates arrive as datetimes, format them as YYYY-MM-DD",
604:         has_time=has_time,
605:     )
606: 
607: 
608: def date_candidates(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> list[DateCandidate]:
609:     """Date range candidates: every column whose values, or name, say date."""
610:     out: list[DateCandidate] = []
611:     for column in frame.columns:
612:         series = frame[column].dropna()
613:         if len(series) == 0:
614:             continue
615:         if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(series):
616:             out.append(datetime_candidate(str(column), series))
617:             continue
618:         texts = series.astype("string").str.strip()
619:         name_hint = any(
620:             hint in canonical_column(str(column)) for hint in DATE_NAME_HINTS
621:         )
622:         if float(texts.str.match(ISO_DATE_RE).mean()) >= MIN_DATE_MATCH_SHARE:
623:             out.append(iso_candidate(str(column), texts))
624:         elif float(texts.str.match(NUMERIC_DATE_RE).mean()) >= MIN_DATE_MATCH_SHARE:
625:             out.append(numeric_date_candidate(str(column), texts))
626:         elif float(texts.str.match(COMPACT_DATE_RE).mean()) >= MIN_DATE_MATCH_SHARE:
627:             out.append(compact_date_candidate(str(column), texts))
628:         elif name_hint:
629:             out.append(name_only_candidate(str(column), texts))
630:     return out
631: 
632: 
633: def date_verdict_text(candidate: DateCandidate) -> str:
634:     """One line verdict: the format plus the order proof."""
635:     if candidate.verdict == "ISO":
636:         return "ISO YYYY-MM-DD, unambiguous"
637:     if candidate.verdict in {"DD/MM", "MM/DD"}:
638:         return f"{candidate.verdict}, {candidate.proof}"
639:     if candidate.verdict == "ambiguous":
640:         return f"ambiguous ({candidate.proof})"
641:     if candidate.verdict == "compact":
642:         return f"compact {candidate.format_label} ({candidate.proof})"
643:     return f"unparsed ({candidate.proof})"
644: 
645: 
646: def has_hint(column: str, hints: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
647:     """Whether the canonical column name contains a hint on token boundaries.
648: 
649:     Token matching keeps "amount_paid" from satisfying the "id" hint: the
650:     hint must start the name or sit between underscores, never inside a word.
651:     """
652:     canonical = canonical_column(column)
653:     for hint in hints:
654:         token = canonical_column(hint)
655:         if (
656:             canonical == token
657:             or canonical.startswith(f"{token}_")
658:             or f"_{token}_" in canonical
659:         ):
660:             return True
661:     return False
662: 
663: 
664: def find_target_column(columns: Sequence[str], hints: Sequence[str]) -> str:
665:     """Best source column for a target: exact canonical match first, then hint."""
666:     exact = {canonical_column(str(column)): str(column) for column in columns}
667:     for hint in hints:
668:         token = canonical_column(hint)
669:         if token in exact:
670:             return exact[token]
671:     for column in columns:
672:         if has_hint(str(column), hints):
673:             return str(column)
674:     return ""
675:

677: @dataclass
678: class SignVerdict:
679:     """How debits and credits are encoded, and what the adapter must do."""
680: 
681:     verdict: str
682:     explanation: str
683:     amount_column: str = ""
684:     debit_column: str = ""
685:     credit_column: str = ""
686:     type_column: str = ""
687: 
688: 
689: def find_type_column(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
690:     """Find a column carrying debit or credit meaning, by name first, then values."""
691:     for column in frame.columns:
692:         if has_hint(str(column), TYPE_NAME_HINTS):
693:             return str(column)
694:     for column in frame.columns:
695:         series = frame[column].dropna()
696:         if len(series) == 0:
697:             continue
698:         if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(series) or pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(series):
699:             continue
700:         if int(series.nunique()) > MAX_TYPE_DISTINCT:
701:             continue
702:         lowered = {str(value).strip().lower() for value in series.unique()}
703:         if lowered & TYPE_VALUE_HINTS:
704:             return str(column)
705:     return ""
706: 
707: 
708: def sign_verdict(frame: pd.DataFrame, numeric: Sequence[NumericCandidate]) -> SignVerdict:
709:     """Classify the sign convention the adapter must reproduce.
710: 
711:     Order matters: a debit/credit column pair is detected by name before the
712:     signed scan, because debit_amount and credit_amount each hold only
713:     positive values and would otherwise read as "positive with type".
714:     """
715:     by_name = {entry.column: entry for entry in numeric}
716:     debit_columns = [name for name in by_name if has_hint(name, DEBIT_NAME_HINTS)]
717:     credit_columns = [name for name in by_name if has_hint(name, CREDIT_NAME_HINTS)]
718:     if debit_columns and credit_columns:
719:         debit_column, credit_column = debit_columns[0], credit_columns[0]
720:         return SignVerdict(
721:             verdict="separate debit/credit columns",
722:             explanation=(
723:                 f"{debit_column} holds debits and {credit_column} holds credits, "
724:                 "so the adapter must fold the pair into one signed amount"
725:             ),
726:             debit_column=debit_column,
727:             credit_column=credit_column,
728:         )
729: 
730:     amount_columns = [name for name in by_name if has_hint(name, AMOUNT_NAME_HINTS)]
731:     if not amount_columns:
732:         amount_columns = [
733:             name
734:             for name, entry in by_name.items()
735:             if not has_hint(name, BALANCE_NAME_HINTS)
736:             and entry.negatives > 0
737:             and entry.positives > 0
738:         ]
739:     signed = [
740:         name
741:         for name in amount_columns
742:         if by_name[name].negatives > 0 and by_name[name].positives > 0
743:     ]
744:     if signed:
745:         entry = by_name[signed[0]]
746:         return SignVerdict(
747:             verdict="single signed amount",
748:             explanation=(
749:                 f"{entry.column} holds {entry.negatives} negative and "
750:                 f"{entry.positives} positive values, so debits are already negative"
751:             ),
752:             amount_column=entry.column,
753:         )
754: 
755:     non_negative = [
756:         name
757:         for name in amount_columns
758:         if by_name[name].negatives == 0 and by_name[name].positives > 0
759:     ]
760:     if non_negative:
761:         type_column = find_type_column(frame)
762:         if type_column:
763:             return SignVerdict(
764:                 verdict="positive amount with type column",
765:                 explanation=(
766:                     f"{non_negative[0]} is all non negative and {type_column} "
767:                     "carries the debit or credit meaning"
768:                 ),
769:                 amount_column=non_negative[0],
770:                 type_column=type_column,
771:             )
772: 
773:     return SignVerdict(
774:         verdict="no sign convention detected",
775:         explanation=(
776:             "no amount column mixes signs and no debit or credit type column "
777:             "was found"
778:         ),
779:     )
780: 
781: 
782: @dataclass
783: class CategoryCandidate:
784:     """A low cardinality text column: a merchant_category stand-in."""
785: 
786:     column: str
787:     distinct: int
788:     top_values: list[tuple[str, int]] = field(default_factory=list)
789: 
790: 
791: def category_candidates(
792:     frame: pd.DataFrame, skip: set[str]
793: ) -> list[CategoryCandidate]:
794:     """Low cardinality text columns with their top value counts.
795: 
796:     Identifier columns (every value unique) and the date candidates are
797:     excluded, and at most MAX_CATEGORY_COLUMNS are reported so a wide file
798:     cannot flood the report.
799:     """
800:     out: list[CategoryCandidate] = []
801:     for column in frame.columns:
802:         if str(column) in skip:
803:             continue
804:         series = frame[column]
805:         if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(series) or pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(series):
806:             continue
807:         if pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(series):
808:             continue
809:         non_null = series.dropna()
810:         if len(non_null) == 0:
811:             continue
812:         distinct = int(non_null.nunique())
813:         if distinct < 2 or distinct > MAX_CATEGORY_DISTINCT:
814:             continue
815:         if distinct == len(non_null):
816:             continue  # every value unique: an identifier, not a category
817:         counts = non_null.astype("string").value_counts().head(TOP_CATEGORY_VALUES)
818:         top = [
819:             (str(value)[:MAX_CELL_WIDTH], int(count)) for value, count in counts.items()
820:         ]
821:         out.append(CategoryCandidate(str(column), distinct, top))
822:         if len(out) >= MAX_CATEGORY_COLUMNS:
823:             break
824:     return out
825: 
826: 
827: def cell_text(value: object) -> str:
828:     """Render one sample cell: truncated, with missing values left blank."""
829:     if value is None or (not isinstance(value, str) and bool(pd.isna(value))):
830:         return ""
831:     text = str(value)
832:     if len(text) > MAX_CELL_WIDTH:
833:         return text[: MAX_CELL_WIDTH - 3] + "..."
834:     return text
835: 
836: 
837: def date_target_detail(candidate: DateCandidate) -> str:
838:     """What the adapter must do with the chosen date column."""
839:     span = f"{candidate.start} to {candidate.end}" if candidate.start else "range unknown"
840:     if candidate.verdict == "ISO":
841:         return f"ISO YYYY-MM-DD, {span}, keep as-is"
842:     if candidate.verdict == "DD/MM":
843:         return f"parse as DD/MM/YYYY, emit YYYY-MM-DD, {span}"
844:     if candidate.verdict == "MM/DD":
845:         return f"parse as MM/DD/YYYY, emit YYYY-MM-DD, {span}"
846:     if candidate.verdict == "ambiguous":
847:         return f"order ambiguous, confirm then emit YYYY-MM-DD, {span}"
848:     if candidate.verdict == "compact":
849:         return f"parse as YYYYMMDD, emit YYYY-MM-DD, {span}"
850:     return candidate.proof
851: 
852: 
853: def verdict_notes(
854:     table: ProbeTable, date_pick: DateCandidate | None, sign: SignVerdict
855: ) -> list[str]:
856:     """The adapter notes column of the VERDICT block, one bullet per rule."""
857:     notes: list[str] = []
858:     if date_pick is not None:
859:         if date_pick.verdict == "DD/MM":
860:             notes.append(
861:                 f"parse {date_pick.column} as DD/MM/YYYY, then emit YYYY-MM-DD "
862:                 "for the builder"
863:             )
864:         elif date_pick.verdict == "MM/DD":
865:             notes.append(
866:                 f"parse {date_pick.column} as MM/DD/YYYY, then emit YYYY-MM-DD "
867:                 "for the builder"
868:             )
869:         elif date_pick.verdict == "ambiguous":
870:             notes.append(
871:                 f"{date_pick.column} date order is ambiguous: confirm it against "
872:                 "a known date (the Canada default is DD/MM) before trusting "
873:                 "the range"
874:             )
875:         elif date_pick.verdict == "compact":
876:             notes.append(
877:                 f"parse {date_pick.column} as YYYYMMDD, then emit YYYY-MM-DD "
878:                 "for the builder"
879:             )
880:         elif date_pick.verdict == "unparsed":
881:             notes.append(
882:                 f"{date_pick.column} did not parse as a date: {date_pick.proof}"
883:             )
884:     if sign.verdict == "separate debit/credit columns":
885:         notes.append(
886:             f"amount = {sign.credit_column} minus {sign.debit_column}, then drop "
887:             "the pair so debits end up negative"
888:         )
889:     elif sign.verdict == "positive amount with type column":
890:         notes.append(
891:             f"pass the {sign.type_column} column through (the builder lets "
892:             "transaction_type win) or negate debit rows"
893:         )
894:     elif sign.verdict == "no sign convention detected":
895:         notes.append(
896:             "run the balance continuity check (docs/research.md step 8) before "
897:             "trusting any sign"
898:         )
899:     if table.encoding == "latin-1":
900:         notes.append("re-encode the file to UTF-8 in the adapter before committing it")
901:     if table.delimiter and table.delimiter != ",":
902:         notes.append(
903:             f"the source delimiter is {DELIMITERS[table.delimiter]}: pass it "
904:             "explicitly when reading"
905:         )
906:     if table.row_sampled:
907:         cap_mb = MAX_INPUT_CSV_BYTES // (1024 * 1024)
908:         notes.append(
909:             f"input exceeds the {cap_mb} MB builder cap: the probe shows the "
910:             f"first {PROBE_ROW_SAMPLE} rows, so aggregate to daily category rows "
911:             "or raise the cap deliberately"
912:         )
913:     notes.append(
914:         "remap the real category labels onto the pipeline set (Dining, "
915:         "Groceries, Retail, Subscriptions, Transit, Travel, Utilities, Income); "
916:         "unknown labels become Other"
917:     )
918:     return notes
919: 
920: 
921: def verdict_lines(
922:     table: ProbeTable,
923:     numeric: Sequence[NumericCandidate],
924:     dates: Sequence[DateCandidate],
925:     sign: SignVerdict,
926:     categories: Sequence[CategoryCandidate],
927: ) -> list[str]:
928:     """The VERDICT block: one line per canonical target, then the notes."""
929:     frame = table.frame
930:     rows = len(frame)
931:     columns = [str(column) for column in frame.columns]
932:     numeric_columns = [entry.column for entry in numeric]
933:     used: set[str] = set()
934:     lines: list[str] = []
935: 
936:     id_column = find_target_column(columns, ID_TARGET_HINTS)
937:     if id_column:
938:         distinct = int(frame[id_column].nunique(dropna=True))
939:         if distinct == rows:
940:             detail = f"{distinct} distinct values"
941:         else:
942:             detail = f"only {distinct} of {rows} rows distinct, deduplicate or synthesize ids"
943:         lines.append(f"  {'transaction_id':<17} -> {id_column} ({detail})")
944:         used.add(id_column)
945:     else:
946:         lines.append(
947:             f"  {'transaction_id':<17} -> MISSING, synthesize TAN style row ids "
948:             "in the adapter (the builder requires it)"
949:         )
950: 
951:     parsed_dates = [entry for entry in dates if entry.verdict != "unparsed"]
952:     pool = list(parsed_dates) if parsed_dates else list(dates)
953:     date_pick = pool[0] if pool else None
954:     if date_pick is not None:
955:         lines.append(
956:             f"  {'date':<17} -> {date_pick.column} ({date_target_detail(date_pick)})"
957:         )
958:         used.add(date_pick.column)
959:     else:
960:         lines.append(
961:             f"  {'date':<17} -> MISSING, no column parses as a date "
962:             "(the builder requires YYYY-MM-DD)"
963:         )
964: 
965:     hour_column = find_target_column(columns, HOUR_TARGET_HINTS)
966:     if hour_column:
967:         lines.append(f"  {'hour':<17} -> {hour_column} (integer hour column, 0 to 23)")
968:         used.add(hour_column)
969:     else:
970:         timed = [entry.column for entry in dates if entry.has_time]
971:         if timed:
972:             lines.append(
973:                 f"  {'hour':<17} -> derive from {timed[0]} (the builder reads the "
974:                 "hour from a timestamp column)"
975:             )
976:             used.add(timed[0])
977:         else:
978:             lines.append(
979:                 f"  {'hour':<17} -> absent, the builder assumes 12 for every row"
980:             )
981: 
982:     if sign.verdict == "separate debit/credit columns":
983:         lines.append(
984:             f"  {'amount':<17} -> fold {sign.debit_column} and {sign.credit_column} "
985:             "into one signed amount column"
986:         )
987:         used.update({sign.debit_column, sign.credit_column})
988:     else:
989:         amount_column = sign.amount_column or find_target_column(
990:             numeric_columns, AMOUNT_TARGET_HINTS
991:         )
992:         if amount_column:
993:             lines.append(
994:                 f"  {'amount':<17} -> {amount_column} ({sign.verdict})"
995:             )
996:             used.add(amount_column)
997:         else:
998:             lines.append(
999:                 f"  {'amount':<17} -> MISSING, no numeric amount column "
1000:                 "(the builder requires it)"
1001:             )
1002: 
1003:     category_pool = [entry.column for entry in categories] or columns
1004:     category_column = find_target_column(category_pool, CATEGORY_TARGET_HINTS)
1005:     if category_column:
1006:         distinct = int(frame[category_column].nunique(dropna=True))
1007:         lines.append(
1008:             f"  {'merchant_category':<17} -> {category_column} ({distinct} distinct labels)"
1009:         )
1010:         used.add(category_column)
1011:     else:
1012:         lines.append(
1013:             f"  {'merchant_category':<17} -> MISSING, pick a low cardinality text "
1014:             "column from the category list above"
1015:         )
1016: 
1017:     balance_column = find_target_column(numeric_columns, BALANCE_TARGET_HINTS)
1018:     if balance_column:
1019:         entry = next(
1020:             (item for item in numeric if item.column == balance_column), None
1021:         )
1022:         detail = f"{entry.minimum:,.2f} to {entry.maximum:,.2f}" if entry else "numeric"
1023:         lines.append(f"  {'account_balance':<17} -> {balance_column} ({detail})")
1024:         used.add(balance_column)
1025:     else:
1026:         lines.append(
1027:             f"  {'account_balance':<17} -> MISSING, the builder needs it for the "
1028:             "balance series and debt horizon"
1029:         )
1030: 
1031:     unused = [column for column in columns if column not in used]
1032:     lines.append(
1033:         f"  {'not mapped':<17} -> {', '.join(unused) if unused else 'none'}"
1034:     )
1035:     lines.append(f"  {'adapter notes':<17} ->")
1036:     for note in verdict_notes(table, date_pick, sign):
1037:         lines.append(f"    - {note}")
1038:     return lines
1039: 
1040: 
1041: def render_report(table: ProbeTable) -> str:
1042:     """Format the whole probe report as one printable string."""
1043:     numeric = numeric_candidates(table.frame)
1044:     dates = date_candidates(table.frame)
1045:     sign = sign_verdict(table.frame, numeric)
1046:     date_columns = {entry.column for entry in dates}
1047:     categories = category_candidates(table.frame, date_columns)
1048: 
1049:     rows, column_count = table.frame.shape
1050:     lines: list[str] = ["probe_schema report"]
1051:     lines.append(f"  file: {rel_to_root(table.path)}")
1052:     lines.append(f"  sha256: {table.checksum}")
1053:     lines.append(
1054:         f"  size: {table.size_bytes:,} bytes ({table.size_bytes / 1024:.1f} kB)"
1055:     )
1056:     lines.append(f"  encoding: {table.encoding or 'not applicable (binary workbook)'}")
1057:     if table.delimiter:
1058:         glyph = "TAB" if table.delimiter == "\t" else table.delimiter
1059:         lines.append(f"  delimiter: {DELIMITERS[table.delimiter]} ({glyph})")
1060:     else:
1061:         lines.append("  delimiter: not applicable (workbook sheet)")
1062:     sampled = ""
1063:     if table.row_sampled:
1064:         cap_mb = MAX_INPUT_CSV_BYTES // (1024 * 1024)
1065:         sampled = (
1066:             f" (first {PROBE_ROW_SAMPLE} rows only, input exceeds the "
1067:             f"{cap_mb} MB builder cap)"
1068:         )
1069:     lines.append(f"  rows: {rows}  columns: {column_count}{sampled}")
1070: 
1071:     lines.append("")
1072:     lines.append("columns (dtype, nulls)")
1073:     shown = [str(column) for column in table.frame.columns][:MAX_REPORTED_COLUMNS]
1074:     for column in shown:
1075:         series = table.frame[column]
1076:         nulls = int(series.isna().sum())
1077:         lines.append(
1078:             f"  {column:<24} {str(series.dtype):<16} nulls {nulls} "
1079:             f"({nulls / rows:.1%})"
1080:         )
1081:     hidden = column_count - len(shown)
1082:     if hidden > 0:
1083:         lines.append(f"  ... and {hidden} more columns (probe shows the first {len(shown)})")
1084: 
1085:     lines.append("")
1086:     lines.append(f"sample rows ({min(SAMPLE_ROWS, rows)} of {rows})")
1087:     display = table.frame.head(SAMPLE_ROWS).map(cell_text)
1088:     for row_line in display.to_string(index=False).splitlines():
1089:         lines.append(f"  {row_line}")
1090: 
1091:     lines.append("")
1092:     lines.append("date range candidates")
1093:     if not dates:
1094:         lines.append("  none: no column parses as a date")
1095:         lines.append(
1096:             "  date format verdict: no date column found, the adapter must "
1097:             "build or decode one"
1098:         )
1099:     else:
1100:         for candidate in dates:
1101:             span = (
1102:                 f"range {candidate.start} to {candidate.end}"
1103:                 if candidate.start
1104:                 else "range unknown"
1105:             )
1106:             lines.append(
1107:                 f"  {candidate.column}: {candidate.matched}/{candidate.total} values "
1108:                 f"match {candidate.format_label}, {span}"
1109:             )
1110:             lines.append(
1111:                 f"    date format verdict: {date_verdict_text(candidate)}"
1112:             )
1113: 
1114:     lines.append("")
1115:     lines.append(f"sign convention verdict: {sign.verdict} ({sign.explanation})")
1116: 
1117:     lines.append("")
1118:     lines.append("numeric candidates for amount/balance")
1119:     if not numeric:
1120:         lines.append("  none: no column parses as numbers or money")
1121:     for entry in numeric[:MAX_REPORTED_COLUMNS]:
1122:         lines.append(
1123:             f"  {entry.column:<24} {entry.minimum:,.2f} to {entry.maximum:,.2f} "
1124:             f"({entry.negatives} negative, {entry.positives} positive)"
1125:         )
1126:     if len(numeric) > MAX_REPORTED_COLUMNS:
1127:         lines.append(f"  ... and {len(numeric) - MAX_REPORTED_COLUMNS} more numeric columns")
1128: 
1129:     lines.append("")
1130:     lines.append(f"category-like columns (top {TOP_CATEGORY_VALUES} values)")
1131:     if not categories:
1132:         lines.append("  none: no low cardinality text column found")
1133:     for entry in categories:
1134:         pairs = ", ".join(f"{value} {count}" for value, count in entry.top_values)
1135:         lines.append(f"  {entry.column} ({entry.distinct} distinct): {pairs}")
1136:     if len(categories) >= MAX_CATEGORY_COLUMNS:
1137:         lines.append(f"  ... (category list capped at {MAX_CATEGORY_COLUMNS} columns)")
1138: 
1139:     lines.append("")
1140:     lines.append("VERDICT (what the tomorrow adapter should map)")
1141:     lines.extend(
1142:         verdict_lines(table, numeric, dates, sign, categories)
1143:     )
1144:     return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
1145: 
1146: 
1147: def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
1148:     """Probe the input file and print the full report."""
1149:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
1150:         description="Probe a tabular file and print its schema verdict"
1151:     )
1152:     parser.add_argument(
1153:         "--input",
1154:         type=Path,
1155:         required=True,
1156:         help="source csv, tsv, or xlsx file (read only, any location)",
1157:     )
1158:     args = parser.parse_args(argv)
1159:     table = read_table(args.input)
1160:     print(render_report(table), end="")
1161:     return 0
1162: 
1163: 
1164: if __name__ == "__main__":
1165:     raise SystemExit(main())

1: # Ledger Odyssey Decision Records
2:

5: ## Nov 04 2026: Phase 0: Stack and gameplay architecture
6: 
7: **Context**: 48-hour solo hackathon with a 24-hour execution budget, static
8: GitHub Pages deliverable, live booth play and a 2-minute demo video, and a
9: "serious analysis wearing a game" judge story demanding non-dashboard viz.
10: 
11: **Decision**: React 19 + R3F 9 + drei + Zustand 5 + Vite 6 (exact versions from
12: the zenith-web and Talon reference repos), offline Python/uv data pipeline to
13: world.json, game logic in a pure TS command bus and reducer, on-rails transfers
14: (no free flight), auto-demo as deterministic command replay, 2.5D Canvas
15: fallback pre-committed at event hour 6.
16: 
17: **Rationale**: Declarative 3D gives the highest wow per hour when scaffolding is
18: copied from two working repos; a pure reducer makes gameplay testable and the
19: auto-demo deterministic; on-rails avoids the physics tuning black hole.
20: 
21: **Trade-offs**: No free-flight feel, no postprocessing on weak GPUs, no deep
22: links, and world.json must be regenerated when the CSV schema shifts. All are
23: acceptable for a 24-hour static deliverable.

## Tangerine dataset preparation research

Research date: 2026-11-06. Phase context: pre-hackathon readiness for the
unknown Tangerine dataset that lands Saturday Nov 7, targeting the
[Tangerine] Best Financial Resilience Challenge track inside the fresh repo
decision. Citations 137 to 157 are listed at the end of this section and do
not repeat citations 1 to 136.

### Sponsor context (verified)

| Fact | Detail | Source | Confidence |
|------|--------|--------|------------|
| Track name and prize | [Tangerine] Best Financial Resilience Challenge, 1 winner, prize listed as "To Be Announced" | Sheridan 2026 Devpost (141) | High |
| Dataset delivery | Event site says Tangerine is "sponsor-backed, own dataset and problem statement", so the schema is not published before the event | sheridandatathon.com (142) | High |
| Timing | Tangerine keynote at the opening ceremony plus a hands on workshop on Saturday; dataset most likely drops at or right after the opening (10:00 AM Saturday) | GDG Sheridan LinkedIn (143), event site (142) | Medium (exact drop time not published) |
| Judge | Matt Clements, CTO @ Tangerine, is listed as a judge; a Scotiabank data scientist (Emilia Zielinska) is also on the judge list | Sheridan 2026 Devpost (141), judge LinkedIn post | High |
| Brand context | Tangerine is a wholly owned Scotiabank subsidiary (ING Direct from 1997, acquired 2012), about 2 million clients, digital only bank | Tangerine llms.txt (145), FAQ page | High |
| Product vocabulary | Money Rules (Stash, Round Up, Tax My Habits, Pay Yourself First), Left to Spend budget tool, Goals, Spending Tracker, Orange Alerts, Credit Score Checker, no fee chequing and savings, cash back Mastercard, TFSA/RSP/RIF, HELOC | Money Rules page (144), llms.txt (145) | High |

Read for us: the track name "Financial Resilience" plus Tangerine's own tool
vocabulary (Left to Spend, Money Rules, Goals) means the dataset is likely to

import csv, statistics, json
from collections import defaultdict

rows_by_acct = defaultdict(list)
with open("data/tangerine/monthly_summary.csv", newline="") as f:
    for pos, row in enumerate(csv.DictReader(f)):
        rows_by_acct[int(row["account_id"])].append((pos, row))

def cents(s): return round(float(s) * 100)

metrics = {}
for acct, rows in rows_by_acct.items():
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r[1]["month"])
    inc = sorted(cents(r[1]["money_in"]) for r in rows)
    out = sorted(cents(r[1]["money_out"]) for r in rows)
    hb  = sorted(cents(r[1]["household_bills"]) for r in rows)
    fr  = sorted(cents(r[1]["household_bills"])+cents(r[1]["insurance"])+cents(r[1]["loan_payments"]) for r in rows)
    last6 = rows[-6:]
    bvals = [cents(r[1]["avg_daily_balance"]) for r in last6]
    I = round(statistics.median(inc)); S = round(statistics.median(out))
    H = round(statistics.median(hb)); F = round(statistics.median(fr))
    B = round(sum(bvals)/len(bvals))
    pos = sorted(r[0] for r in rows)
    metrics[acct] = dict(I=I, S=S, H=H, F=F, B=B, n=len(rows), nrows=len(bvals), rowRef=[pos[0], pos[-1]])

loans = {}
with open("data/tangerine/loans.csv", newline="") as f:
    for pos, row in enumerate(csv.DictReader(f)):
        loans[int(row["account_id"])] = (pos, row)

def loan_info(acct):
    if acct in loans:
        pos, row = loans[acct]
        p = round(float(row["monthly_payment"]) * 100) if row["status"] in ("C","D") else 0
        return p, pos, row["status"]
    return 0, None, None

def runway(B, S, I, one_off=0):
    bl = B - one_off; gap = S - I
    if bl <= 0: return 0
    if gap <= 0: return "no shortfall (120+)"
    t = (20*bl + gap)//(2*gap); t = min(t, 1200)
    return t/10.0

gold = {}
for acct in (55447, 32078, 20133, 20111, 20143, 24310):
    m = metrics[acct]; p, lrow, st = loan_info(acct)
    fr_nonzero = sum(1 for r in rows_by_acct[acct] if round(float(r[1]["household_bills"])*100)+round(float(r[1]["insurance"])*100)+round(float(r[1]["loan_payments"])*100) != 0)
    gold[acct] = dict(I=m["I"], F=m["F"], S=m["S"], B=m["B"], H=m["H"], P=p,
                      bufferRowCount=m["nrows"], months=m["n"], rowRef=m["rowRef"],
                      loanRow=lrow, status=st, baseRunway=runway(m["B"], m["S"], m["I"]),
                      frNonzeroMonths=fr_nonzero)
print(json.dumps(gold, indent=1))
# sanity: verify a couple of hand calcs
g=gold[24310]; print("24310 gap:", g["S"]-g["I"], "ratio:", g["B"]/(g["S"]-g["I"]))
g=gold[20111]; print("20111 gap:", g["S"]-g["I"], "ratio:", g["B"]/(g["S"]-g["I"]))
g=gold[20143]; print("20143 gap:", g["S"]-g["I"], "ratio:", g["B"]/(g["S"]-g["I"]))
EOF

def verify_checksums(data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR, sums_path: Path = SUMS_PATH) -> dict[str, str]:
    if not sums_path.is_file():
        raise ChecksumError(f"checksum manifest not found: {rel_to_root(sums_path)}")
    expected: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line_no, line in enumerate(sums_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line: continue
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) != 2 or len(parts[0]) !=64:
            raise ChecksumError(f"{rel_to_root(sums_path)} line {line_no}: expected '<sha256>  <path>'")
        digest, listed = parts
        expected[Path(listed).name] = digest.lower()
    problems = []
    actual = {}
    for name, digest in sorted(expected.items()):
        path = data_dir / name
        if not path.is_file():
            problems.append(f"missing data file: {rel_to_root(path)}"); continue
        got = sha256_file(path)
        actual[name] = got
        if got != digest:
            problems.append(f"checksum mismatch: {name} expected {digest} got {got}")
    if problems:
        raise ChecksumError("; ".join(problems))
    return actual
```

def verify_checksums(data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR, sums_path: Path = SUMS_PATH) -> dict[str, str]:
    if not sums_path.is_file():
        raise ChecksumError(f"checksum manifest not found: {rel_to_root(sums_path)}")
    expected: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line_no, line in enumerate(sums_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line: continue
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) != 2 or len(parts[0]) !=64:
            raise ChecksumError(f"{rel_to_root(sums_path)} line {line_no}: expected '<sha256>  <path>'")
        digest, listed = parts
        expected[Path(listed).name] = digest.lower()
    problems = []
    actual = {}
    for name, digest in sorted(expected.items()):
        path = data_dir / name
        if not path.is_file():

        raise ChecksumError("; ".join(problems))

* verify every file against data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS before reading

* read the eight small tables whole with explicit dtypes and convert money
  columns to integer cents immediately, so no downstream math ever sees a
  float dollar;
* profile transactions.csv (102 MB) in chunked reads for the data quality
  report instead of loading it whole;
* extract daily change-point closes from transactions.csv with chunked
  reading, also never loading the whole file into one DataFrame.

The chunked transactions reader deliberately bypasses the
MAX_INPUT_CSV_BYTES (50 MB) cap in scripts/pipeline_lib.py: that cap guards
build_world's whole-file pd.read_csv, while this reader streams with
read_csv(chunksize=...) and holds one chunk at a time. The cap constant is
never edited.

Run from the repository root for the standalone quality report:

    uv run python -m scripts.engine.load

@dataclass
class DataSet:
    """The loaded tables plus checksums and the data quality report.

    transactions.csv is deliberately absent from tables: it is profiled and
    aggregated in chunked reads and never held as one DataFrame.
    """

    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]
    checksums: dict[str, str]
    quality: dict[str, Any]


def verify_checksums(
    data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR, sums_path: Path = SUMS_PATH
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {filename: sha256} after checking every file in the manifest.

    Raises ChecksumError listing every missing or mismatched file at once,
    so a corrupted copy fails loudly instead of silently feeding metrics.
    The manifest stores repository relative paths; only the file name is
    resolved inside data_dir, which lets tests point the same function at a
    temp copy without touching the real data.
    """
    if not sums_path.is_file():
        raise ChecksumError(f"checksum manifest not found: {rel_to_root(sums_path)}")
    expected: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line_number, line in enumerate(
        sums_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1
    ):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        parts = stripped.split()
        if len(parts) != 2 or len(parts[0]) != 64:
            raise ChecksumError(
                f"{rel_to_root(sums_path)} line {line_number}: "
                "expected '<sha256>  <path>'"
            )
        digest, listed_path = parts
        expected[Path(listed_path).name] = digest.lower()
    if not expected:
        raise ChecksumError(f"{rel_to_root(sums_path)} lists no files")
    problems: list[str] = []
    actual: dict[str, str] = {}
    for name in sorted(expected):
        path = data_dir / name
        if not path.is_file():
            problems.append(f"missing data file: {rel_to_root(path)}")
            continue
        digest = sha256_file(path)
        actual[name] = digest
        if digest != expected[name]:
            problems.append(
                f"checksum mismatch: {name} expected {expected[name]} got {digest}"
            )
    if problems:
        raise ChecksumError("; ".join(problems))
    return actual


def convert_money(frame: pd.DataFrame, table_name: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Convert the table's money columns from float dollars to int cents."""
    columns = MONEY_COLUMNS[table_name]
    nulls = [column for column in columns if frame[column].isna().any()]
    if nulls:
        raise DataError(
            f"{table_name}: money columns contain nulls, cannot convert to "
            f"integer cents: {', '.join(nulls)}"
        )
    for column in columns:
        dollars = frame[column].to_numpy(dtype="float64")
        frame[column] = np.rint(dollars * 100.0).astype("int64")
    return frame


def date_ranges(frame: pd.DataFrame, table_name: str) -> dict[str, list[str | None]]:
    """Min and max of the table's date like columns (strings, ISO order)."""
    ranges: dict[str, list[str | None]] = {}
    for column in DATE_RANGE_COLUMNS.get(table_name, ()):
        if column not in frame.columns:
            continue
        values = frame[column]
        non_null = values[values.notna()]
        if len(non_null) == 0:
            ranges[column] = [None, None]
        else:
            ranges[column] = [str(non_null.min()), str(non_null.max())]
    return ranges


def summarize_frame(frame: pd.DataFrame, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Row count, column count, null counts, and date ranges for one table."""
    return {
        "rows": int(len(frame)),
        "columns": int(frame.shape[1]),
        "nullCounts": {
            str(column): int(count)
            for column, count in frame.isna().sum().items()
            if int(count) > 0
        },
        "dateRanges": date_ranges(frame, table_name),
    }


def profile_transactions(path: Path, chunksize: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Profile transactions.csv in chunked reads without loading it whole."""
    null_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    rows = 0
    date_min: str | None = None
    date_max: str | None = None
    accounts: set[int] = set()
    for chunk in pd.read_csv(path, dtype=TABLE_DTYPES["transactions.csv"], chunksize=chunksize):
        rows += int(len(chunk))
        for column, count in chunk.isna().sum().items():
            if int(count) > 0:
                null_counts[str(column)] = null_counts.get(str(column), 0) + int(count)
        dates = chunk["date"]
        chunk_min, chunk_max = str(dates.min()), str(dates.max())
        date_min = chunk_min if date_min is None else min(date_min, chunk_min)
        date_max = chunk_max if date_max is None else max(date_max, chunk_max)
        accounts.update(int(value) for value in chunk["account_id"].unique())
    return {
        "rows": rows,
        "columns": len(TABLE_DTYPES["transactions.csv"]),
        "nullCounts": null_counts,
        "dateRanges": {"date": [date_min, date_max]},
        "distinctAccounts": len(accounts),
        "readMode": f"chunked, {chunksize} rows per chunk",
    }


def build_derived_quality(
    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], table_quality: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Cross table facts the challenge brief asks the report to show."""
    from scripts.engine.metrics import END_OF_2025_LABEL

    accounts = tables["accounts.csv"]
    monthly = tables["monthly_summary.csv"]
    loans = tables["loans.csv"]
    status_counts = (
        loans["status"]
        .value_counts()
        .reindex(["A", "B", "C", "D"])
        .fillna(0)
        .astype("int64")
    )
    running_mask = loans["status"].isin(RUNNING_STATUS_RULE)
    transactions_quality = table_quality["transactions.csv"]
    return {
        "accountsTotal": int(len(accounts)),
        "accountsWithMonthlyRows": int(monthly["account_id"].nunique()),
        "monthlyMonthRange": table_quality["monthly_summary.csv"]["dateRanges"].get(
            "month"
        ),
        "transactionsDateRange": transactions_quality["dateRanges"].get("date"),
        "transactionsDistinctAccounts": int(
            transactions_quality.get("distinctAccounts", 0)
        ),
        "loansTotal": int(len(loans)),
        "loansStatusCounts": {
            str(status): int(count) for status, count in status_counts.items()
        },
        "loansRunningAtEnd2025": int(running_mask.sum()),
        "loansRunningRule": (
            f"status in {'/'.join(sorted(RUNNING_STATUS_RULE))} counts as running "
            f"at {END_OF_2025_LABEL}"
        ),
    }


def load_dataset(
    data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR, sums_path: Path = SUMS_PATH, chunksize: int = TRANSACTIONS_CHUNK_ROWS
) -> DataSet:
    """Verify checksums, read every table with explicit dtypes, build quality."""
    checksums = verify_checksums(data_dir, sums_path)
    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    table_quality: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for table_name in TABLE_NAMES:
        path = data_dir / table_name
        if table_name == "transactions.csv":
            table_quality[table_name] = profile_transactions(path, chunksize)
            continue
        frame = pd.read_csv(path, dtype=TABLE_DTYPES[table_name])
        table_quality[table_name] = summarize_frame(frame, table_name)
        if table_name in MONEY_COLUMNS:
            frame = convert_money(frame, table_name)
        tables[table_name] = frame
    quality: dict[str, Any] = {
        "checksumsVerified": True,
        "checksumManifest": rel_to_root(sums_path),
        "tables": table_quality,
        "derived": build_derived_quality(tables, table_quality),
    }
    return DataSet(tables=tables, checksums=checksums, quality=quality)


def extract_daily_closes(
    monthly: pd.DataFrame,
    transactions_path: Path | None = None,
    chunksize: int = TRANSACTIONS_CHUNK_ROWS,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Aggregate transactions.csv into per-account daily change-point closes.

    Returns a DataFrame with columns account_id, date, close_cents sorted by
    account then date, keeping only dates where the balance changes (the
    first date of each account is always kept to anchor the series).

    Method: sum signed_amount into integer cents per (account, date), cumsum
    per account, then anchor the per-account constant from the LAST row of
    monthly_summary (month_end_balance minus cumulative nets through that
    month, with quiet months forward filled). The anchor makes the series
    end exactly on the bank's published month end balance; the residual
    disagreement between the two source files is a few cents because the
    sources carry independent rounding, documented in docs/decisions.md.

    Bypasses MAX_INPUT_CSV_BYTES on purpose: this reader streams with
    chunksize and never loads transactions.csv whole.
    """
    if transactions_path is None:
        transactions_path = DATA_DIR / "transactions.csv"
    net_parts: list[pd.Series] = []
    for chunk in pd.read_csv(
        transactions_path,
        usecols=["account_id", "date", "signed_amount"],
        chunksize=chunksize,
    ):
        signed_cents = np.rint(chunk["signed_amount"].to_numpy(dtype="float64") * 100.0)
        chunk = chunk.assign(net=signed_cents.astype("int64"))
        net_parts.append(
            chunk.groupby(["account_id", "date"], sort=False)["net"].sum()
        )
    if not net_parts:
        raise DataError(f"{rel_to_root(transactions_path)} produced no rows")
    daily = pd.concat(net_parts).sort_index()
    daily.index.names = ["account_id", "date"]
    daily = daily.reset_index().sort_values(
        ["account_id", "date"], kind="stable"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)
    daily["cum"] = daily.groupby("account_id")["net"].cumsum()
    daily["ym"] = daily["date"].str[:7]

    # Cumulative nets at each monthly_summary month end, quiet months
    # forward filled, then the anchor constant from each account's last row.
    month_last = daily.groupby(["account_id", "ym"], sort=False).tail(1)
    month_last = month_last[["account_id", "ym", "cum"]].rename(columns={"ym": "month"})
    months = monthly[["account_id", "month"]].sort_values(
        ["account_id", "month"], kind="stable"
    )
    cum_at_month_end = months.merge(month_last, on=["account_id", "month"], how="left")
    cum_at_month_end["cum"] = (
        cum_at_month_end.groupby("account_id")["cum"].ffill().fillna(0.0)
    )
    last_month_cum = (
        cum_at_month_end.groupby("account_id", sort=False).tail(1)[
            ["account_id", "cum"]
        ]
    )
    last_month = (
        monthly.sort_values(["account_id", "month"], kind="stable")
        .groupby("account_id", sort=False)
        .tail(1)[["account_id", "month", "month_end_balance"]]
    )
    anchor = last_month.merge(last_month_cum, on="account_id", how="left")
    if anchor["cum"].isna().any():
        missing = sorted(int(value) for value in anchor.loc[anchor["cum"].isna(), "account_id"])
        raise DataError(
            "accounts with no transaction days for their last monthly row: "
            f"{missing[:10]}"
        )
    anchor["init"] = anchor["month_end_balance"] - anchor["cum"]
    daily = daily.merge(anchor[["account_id", "init"]], on="account_id", how="left")
    if daily["init"].isna().any():
        missing = sorted(
            int(value) for value in daily.loc[daily["init"].isna(), "account_id"].unique()
        )
        raise DataError(
            "accounts in transactions.csv without a monthly_summary anchor: "
            f"{missing[:10]}"
        )
    daily["close"] = daily["init"] + daily["cum"]

    # Change points only: keep each account's first date, then only dates
    # whose net moved the balance (zero net days repeat the prior close).
    first_in_account = ~daily.duplicated("account_id", keep="first")
    keep = first_in_account | (daily["net"] != 0)
    closes = daily.loc[keep, ["account_id", "date", "close"]].rename(
        columns={"close": "close_cents"}
    )
    return closes.reset_index(drop=True)


def quality_lines(quality: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Human readable data quality report lines for the build stdout."""
    lines = [
        "data quality",
        f"  checksums: all files match {quality['checksumManifest']}",
    ]
    for table_name, summary in quality["tables"].items():
        nulls = summary["nullCounts"]
        null_text = ", ".join(
            f"{column}={count}" for column, count in sorted(nulls.items())
        )
        if not null_text:
            null_text = "none"
        mode = summary.get("readMode", "whole file")
        lines.append(
            f"  {table_name}: {summary['rows']:,} rows, "
            f"{summary['columns']} columns, nulls: {null_text} ({mode})"
        )
        for column, span in summary["dateRanges"].items():
            lines.append(f"    {column}: {span[0]} to {span[1]}")
    derived = quality["derived"]
    lines.append(
        f"  accounts: {derived['accountsTotal']:,} total, "
        f"{derived['accountsWithMonthlyRows']:,} with monthly_summary rows "
        f"(months {derived['monthlyMonthRange'][0]} to "
        f"{derived['monthlyMonthRange'][1]})"
    )
    lines.append(
        f"  transactions: {derived['transactionsDistinctAccounts']:,} distinct "
        f"accounts, dates {derived['transactionsDateRange'][0]} to "
        f"{derived['transactionsDateRange'][1]}"
    )
    status = derived["loansStatusCounts"]
    lines.append(
        "  loans: "
        + ", ".join(f"{key}={status[key]}" for key in ("A", "B", "C", "D"))
        + f", running at end of 2025: {derived['loansRunningAtEnd2025']} "
        f"({derived['loansRunningRule']})"
    )
    return lines


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Print the checksum verdict and the data quality report."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Verify Tangerine checksums and print the quality report"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", type=Path, default=DATA_DIR)
    parser.add_argument("--sums", type=Path, default=SUMS_PATH)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        dataset = load_dataset(args.data_dir, args.sums)
    except (ChecksumError, DataError) as error:
        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for line in quality_lines(dataset.quality):
        print(line)
    print("scripts.engine.load: PASS")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Load the nine Tangerine CSVs with verified checksums and explicit dtypes.

Responsibilities:

* verify every file against data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS before reading
  (ChecksumError lists every mismatch in one loud message);
* read the eight small tables whole with explicit dtypes and convert money
  columns to integer cents immediately, so no downstream math ever sees a
  float dollar;
* profile transactions.csv (102 MB) in chunked reads for the data quality
  report instead of loading it whole;
* extract daily change-point closes from transactions.csv with chunked
  reading, also never loading the whole file into one DataFrame.

The chunked transactions reader deliberately bypasses the
MAX_INPUT_CSV_BYTES (50 MB) cap in scripts/pipeline_lib.py: that cap guards
build_world's whole-file pd.read_csv, while this reader streams with
read_csv(chunksize=...) and holds one chunk at a time. The cap constant is
never edited.

Run from the repository root for the standalone quality report:

    uv run python -m scripts.engine.load
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, NoReturn, Sequence

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from scripts.engine.metrics import RUNNING_STATUS_RULE
from scripts.pipeline_lib import REPO_ROOT, rel_to_root, sha256_file

DATA_DIR: Path = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "tangerine"
SUMS_PATH: Path = DATA_DIR / "SHA256SUMS"

# One chunk of transactions.csv at a time: ~300k rows keeps peak memory flat
# regardless of the file growing.
TRANSACTIONS_CHUNK_ROWS: int = 300_000

TABLE_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "accounts.csv",
    "cards.csv",
    "clients.csv",
    "dispositions.csv",
    "districts.csv",
    "loans.csv",
    "monthly_summary.csv",
    "standing_orders.csv",
    "transactions.csv",
)


class ChecksumError(RuntimeError):
    """A data file does not match data/tangerine/SHA256SUMS."""


class DataError(RuntimeError):
    """The loaded data violates an assumption the engine relies on."""


# Explicit dtypes for every column of every CSV. Dates, months, and account
# numbers at partner banks stay strings: ISO text sorts and slices without
# parsing and never loses leading zeros.
TABLE_DTYPES: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {
    "accounts.csv": {
        "account_id": "int64",
        "district_id": "int64",
        "frequency": "str",
        "account_opened": "str",
    },
    "cards.csv": {
        "card_id": "int64",
        "disposition_id": "int64",
        "card_type": "str",
        "issued": "str",
    },
    "clients.csv": {
        "client_id": "int64",
        "gender": "str",
        "birth_date": "str",
        "district_id": "int64",
    },
    "dispositions.csv": {
        "disposition_id": "int64",
        "client_id": "int64",
        "account_id": "int64",
        "type": "str",
    },
    # District 69 has no 2022 unemployment or crime values (brief data
    # dictionary), so those two columns are nullable floats.
    "districts.csv": {
        "district_id": "int64",
        "district_name": "str",
        "region": "str",
        "inhabitants": "int64",
        "municipalities_under_500": "int64",
        "municipalities_500_1999": "int64",
        "municipalities_2000_9999": "int64",
        "municipalities_over_10000": "int64",
        "num_cities": "int64",
        "urban_ratio_pct": "float64",
        "average_salary": "float64",
        "unemployment_rate_2022": "float64",
        "unemployment_rate_2023": "float64",
        "entrepreneurs_per_1000": "int64",
        "crimes_2022": "float64",
        "crimes_2023": "int64",
    },
    "loans.csv": {
        "loan_id": "int64",
        "account_id": "int64",
        "loan_start": "str",
        "amount": "float64",
        "duration_months": "int64",
        "monthly_payment": "float64",
        "status": "str",
        "status_meaning": "str",
        "defaulted": "int64",
    },
    "monthly_summary.csv": {
        "account_id": "int64",
        "month": "str",
        "money_in": "float64",
        "money_out": "float64",
        "cash_deposits": "float64",
        "transfers_in": "float64",
        "pension_in": "float64",
        "interest_in": "float64",
        "household_bills": "float64",
        "insurance": "float64",
        "loan_payments": "float64",
        "bank_fees": "float64",
        "cash_withdrawals_genuine": "float64",
        "card_withdrawals": "float64",
        "transfers_out_other": "float64",
        "month_end_balance": "float64",
        "min_balance": "float64",
        "avg_daily_balance": "float64",
        "days_below_zero": "int64",
    },
    "standing_orders.csv": {
        "order_id": "int64",
        "account_id": "int64",
        "to_bank": "str",
        "to_account": "str",

        "purpose": "str",
    },
    "transactions.csv": {
        "transaction_id": "int64",
        "account_id": "int64",
        "date": "str",
        "direction": "str",
        "operation": "str",
        "purpose": "str",
        "amount": "float64",
        "signed_amount": "float64",
        "balance": "float64",
        "partner_bank": "str",
        "partner_account": "str",
    },
}

# Money columns converted to integer cents right after reading. Every one of
# them must be null free, which convert_money enforces loudly.
MONEY_COLUMNS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    "loans.csv": ("amount", "monthly_payment"),
    "monthly_summary.csv": (
        "money_in",
        "money_out",
        "cash_deposits",
        "transfers_in",
        "pension_in",
        "interest_in",
        "household_bills",
        "insurance",
        "loan_payments",
        "bank_fees",
        "cash_withdrawals_genuine",
        "card_withdrawals",
        "transfers_out_other",
        "month_end_balance",
        "min_balance",
        "avg_daily_balance",
    ),
    "standing_orders.csv": ("amount",),
}

# Date-like columns included in the per table quality ranges. monthly uses
# YYYY-MM month strings, which sort lexicographically in calendar order.
DATE_RANGE_COLUMNS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    "accounts.csv": ("account_opened",),
    "cards.csv": ("issued",),
    "clients.csv": ("birth_date",),
    "loans.csv": ("loan_start",),
    "monthly_summary.csv": ("month",),
    "transactions.csv": ("date",),
}


@dataclass
class DataSet:
    """The loaded tables plus checksums and the data quality report.

    transactions.csv is deliberately absent from tables: it is profiled and
    aggregated in chunked reads and never held as one DataFrame.
    """

    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]
    checksums: dict[str, str]
    quality: dict[str, Any]


def verify_checksums(
    data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR, sums_path: Path = SUMS_PATH
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {filename: sha256} after checking every file in the manifest.

    Raises ChecksumError listing every missing or mismatched file at once,
    so a corrupted copy fails loudly instead of silently feeding metrics.
    The manifest stores repository relative paths; only the file name is
    resolved inside data_dir, which lets tests point the same function at a
    temp copy without touching the real data.
    """
    if not sums_path.is_file():
        raise ChecksumError(f"checksum manifest not found: {rel_to_root(sums_path)}")
    expected: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line_number, line in enumerate(
        sums_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1
    ):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        parts = stripped.split()
        if len(parts) != 2 or len(parts[0]) != 64:
            raise ChecksumError(
                f"{rel_to_root(sums_path)} line {line_number}: "
                "expected '<sha256>  <path>'"
            )
        digest, listed_path = parts
        expected[Path(listed_path).name] = digest.lower()
    if not expected:
        raise ChecksumError(f"{rel_to_root(sums_path)} lists no files")
    problems: list[str] = []
    actual: dict[str, str] = {}
    for name in sorted(expected):
        path = data_dir / name
        if not path.is_file():
            problems.append(f"missing data file: {rel_to_root(path)}")
            continue
        digest = sha256_file(path)
        actual[name] = digest
        if digest != expected[name]:
            problems.append(
                f"checksum mismatch: {name} expected {expected[name]} got {digest}"
            )
    if problems:
        raise ChecksumError("; ".join(problems))
    return actual


def convert_money(frame: pd.DataFrame, table_name: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Convert the table's money columns from float dollars to int cents."""
    columns = MONEY_COLUMNS[table_name]
    nulls = [column for column in columns if frame[column].isna().any()]
    if nulls:
        raise DataError(
            f"{table_name}: money columns contain nulls, cannot convert to "
            f"integer cents: {', '.join(nulls)}"
        )
    for column in columns:
        dollars = frame[column].to_numpy(dtype="float64")
        frame[column] = np.rint(dollars * 100.0).astype("int64")
    return frame


def date_ranges(frame: pd.DataFrame, table_name: str) -> dict[str, list[str | None]]:
    """Min and max of the table's date like columns (strings, ISO order)."""
    ranges: dict[str, list[str | None]] = {}
    for column in DATE_RANGE_COLUMNS.get(table_name, ()):
        if column not in frame.columns:
            continue
        values = frame[column]
        non_null = values[values.notna()]
        if len(non_null) == 0:
            ranges[column] = [None, None]
        else:
            ranges[column] = [str(non_null.min()), str(non_null.max())]
    return ranges


def summarize_frame(frame: pd.DataFrame, table_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Row count, column count, null counts, and date ranges for one table."""
    return {
        "rows": int(len(frame)),
        "columns": int(frame.shape[1]),
        "nullCounts": {
            str(column): int(count)
            for column, count in frame.isna().sum().items()
            if int(count) > 0
        },
        "dateRanges": date_ranges(frame, table_name),
    }


def profile_transactions(path: Path, chunksize: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Profile transactions.csv in chunked reads without loading it whole."""
    null_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    rows = 0
    date_min: str | None = None
    date_max: str | None = None
    accounts: set[int] = set()
    for chunk in pd.read_csv(path, dtype=TABLE_DTYPES["transactions.csv"], chunksize=chunksize):
        rows += int(len(chunk))
        for column, count in chunk.isna().sum().items():
            if int(count) > 0:
                null_counts[str(column)] = null_counts.get(str(column), 0) + int(count)
        dates = chunk["date"]
        chunk_min, chunk_max = str(dates.min()), str(dates.max())
        date_min = chunk_min if date_min is None else min(date_min, chunk_min)
        date_max = chunk_max if date_max is None else max(date_max, chunk_max)
        accounts.update(int(value) for value in chunk["account_id"].unique())
    return {
        "rows": rows,
        "columns": len(TABLE_DTYPES["transactions.csv"]),
        "nullCounts": null_counts,
        "dateRanges": {"date": [date_min, date_max]},
        "distinctAccounts": len(accounts),
        "readMode": f"chunked, {chunksize} rows per chunk",
    }


def build_derived_quality(
    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], table_quality: dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Cross table facts the challenge brief asks the report to show."""
    from scripts.engine.metrics import END_OF_2025_LABEL

    accounts = tables["accounts.csv"]
    monthly = tables["monthly_summary.csv"]
    loans = tables["loans.csv"]
    status_counts = (
        loans["status"]
        .value_counts()
        .reindex(["A", "B", "C", "D"])
        .fillna(0)
        .astype("int64")
    )
    running_mask = loans["status"].isin(RUNNING_STATUS_RULE)
    transactions_quality = table_quality["transactions.csv"]
    return {
        "accountsTotal": int(len(accounts)),
        "accountsWithMonthlyRows": int(monthly["account_id"].nunique()),
        "monthlyMonthRange": table_quality["monthly_summary.csv"]["dateRanges"].get(
            "month"
        ),
        "transactionsDateRange": transactions_quality["dateRanges"].get("date"),
        "transactionsDistinctAccounts": int(
            transactions_quality.get("distinctAccounts", 0)
        ),
        "loansTotal": int(len(loans)),
        "loansStatusCounts": {
            str(status): int(count) for status, count in status_counts.items()
        },
        "loansRunningAtEnd2025": int(running_mask.sum()),
        "loansRunningRule": (
            f"status in {'/'.join(sorted(RUNNING_STATUS_RULE))} counts as running "
            f"at {END_OF_2025_LABEL}"
        ),
    }


def load_dataset(
    data_dir: Path = DATA_DIR, sums_path: Path = SUMS_PATH, chunksize: int = TRANSACTIONS_CHUNK_ROWS
) -> DataSet:
    """Verify checksums, read every table with explicit dtypes, build quality."""
    checksums = verify_checksums(data_dir, sums_path)
    tables: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}
    table_quality: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for table_name in TABLE_NAMES:
        path = data_dir / table_name
        if table_name == "transactions.csv":
            table_quality[table_name] = profile_transactions(path, chunksize)
            continue
        frame = pd.read_csv(path, dtype=TABLE_DTYPES[table_name])
        table_quality[table_name] = summarize_frame(frame, table_name)
        if table_name in MONEY_COLUMNS:
            frame = convert_money(frame, table_name)
        tables[table_name] = frame
    quality: dict[str, Any] = {
        "checksumsVerified": True,
        "checksumManifest": rel_to_root(sums_path),
        "tables": table_quality,
        "derived": build_derived_quality(tables, table_quality),
    }
    return DataSet(tables=tables, checksums=checksums, quality=quality)


def extract_daily_closes(
    monthly: pd.DataFrame,
    transactions_path: Path | None = None,
    chunksize: int = TRANSACTIONS_CHUNK_ROWS,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Aggregate transactions.csv into per-account daily change-point closes.

    Returns a DataFrame with columns account_id, date, close_cents sorted by
    account then date, keeping only dates where the balance changes (the
    first date of each account is always kept to anchor the series).

    Method: sum signed_amount into integer cents per (account, date), cumsum
    per account, then anchor the per-account constant from the LAST row of
    monthly_summary (month_end_balance minus cumulative nets through that
    month, with quiet months forward filled). The anchor makes the series
    end exactly on the bank's published month end balance; the residual
    disagreement between the two source files is a few cents because the
    sources carry independent rounding, documented in docs/decisions.md.

    Bypasses MAX_INPUT_CSV_BYTES on purpose: this reader streams with
    chunksize and never loads transactions.csv whole.
    """
    if transactions_path is None:
        transactions_path = DATA_DIR / "transactions.csv"
    net_parts: list[pd.Series] = []
    for chunk in pd.read_csv(
        transactions_path,
        usecols=["account_id", "date", "signed_amount"],
        chunksize=chunksize,
    ):
        signed_cents = np.rint(chunk["signed_amount"].to_numpy(dtype="float64") * 100.0)
        chunk = chunk.assign(net=signed_cents.astype("int64"))
        net_parts.append(
            chunk.groupby(["account_id", "date"], sort=False)["net"].sum()
        )
    if not net_parts:
        raise DataError(f"{rel_to_root(transactions_path)} produced no rows")
    daily = pd.concat(net_parts).sort_index()
    daily.index.names = ["account_id", "date"]
    daily = daily.reset_index().sort_values(
        ["account_id", "date"], kind="stable"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)
    daily["cum"] = daily.groupby("account_id")["net"].cumsum()
    daily["ym"] = daily["date"].str[:7]

    # Cumulative nets at each monthly_summary month end, quiet months
    # forward filled, then the anchor constant from each account's last row.
    month_last = daily.groupby(["account_id", "ym"], sort=False).tail(1)
    month_last = month_last[["account_id", "ym", "cum"]].rename(columns={"ym": "month"})
    months = monthly[["account_id", "month"]].sort_values(
        ["account_id", "month"], kind="stable"
    )
    cum_at_month_end = months.merge(month_last, on=["account_id", "month"], how="left")
    cum_at_month_end["cum"] = (
        cum_at_month_end.groupby("account_id")["cum"].ffill().fillna(0.0)
    )
    last_month_cum = (
        cum_at_month_end.groupby("account_id", sort=False).tail(1)[
            ["account_id", "cum"]
        ]
    )
    last_month = (
        monthly.sort_values(["account_id", "month"], kind="stable")
        .groupby("account_id", sort=False)
        .tail(1)[["account_id", "month", "month_end_balance"]]
    )
    anchor = last_month.merge(last_month_cum, on="account_id", how="left")
    if anchor["cum"].isna().any():
        missing = sorted(int(value) for value in anchor.loc[anchor["cum"].isna(), "account_id"])
        raise DataError(
            "accounts with no transaction days for their last monthly row: "
            f"{missing[:10]}"
        )
    anchor["init"] = anchor["month_end_balance"] - anchor["cum"]
    daily = daily.merge(anchor[["account_id", "init"]], on="account_id", how="left")
    if daily["init"].isna().any():
        missing = sorted(
            int(value) for value in daily.loc[daily["init"].isna(), "account_id"].unique()
        )
        raise DataError(
            "accounts in transactions.csv without a monthly_summary anchor: "
            f"{missing[:10]}"
        )
    daily["close"] = daily["init"] + daily["cum"]

    # Change points only: keep each account's first date, then only dates
    # whose net moved the balance (zero net days repeat the prior close).
    first_in_account = ~daily.duplicated("account_id", keep="first")
    keep = first_in_account | (daily["net"] != 0)
    closes = daily.loc[keep, ["account_id", "date", "close"]].rename(
        columns={"close": "close_cents"}
    )
    return closes.reset_index(drop=True)


def quality_lines(quality: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Human readable data quality report lines for the build stdout."""
    lines = [
        "data quality",
        f"  checksums: all files match {quality['checksumManifest']}",
    ]
